# Pragma Research Packet

This file provides a compact machine-readable map for research assistants, indexing systems, and readers who need the source hierarchy.

## Summary

Pragma Research is a frontier mathematics company that works on physics, artificial general intelligence and the nature of reality. The physics program develops Observer Patch Holography (OPH), a proven implementation of simulation theory that reverse engineers the hardware and software generating our observations and the universe: https://floatingpragma.io/physics/. The AGI program develops Cadence, an open-source library researching general intelligence through overlap consensus, equilibrium detuning and functional self-reflection, where learning runs on local activity contrasts with no backward pass: https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/. Investors: https://floatingpragma.io/#investors.

OPH asks whether bounded observers can form a shared physical account from local records, overlap comparison, and repair. The flagship preprint is on PhilPapers: https://philpapers.org/rec/MUEFOC.

An OPH technology surface instantiates observer-like self-reading structure: a bounded physical or software patch has local state, ports or a boundary, readback, records, feedback or repair moves, and an evidence bundle that another party can inspect.

The public research distinguishes exact finite mathematics from physical interpretation. A finite theorem does not by itself establish that its objects are laboratory events, fields, currents, clocks, or scales. Simulations provide reproducible evidence about the stated finite models; exploratory lanes are not physical derivations.

## Release r2022

Release date: 20 August 2026.

The flagship paper is "Finite Observer Consensus as a Reconstruction Principle: Normal Forms, the Standard Model Lie Type, and a Route to the Einstein Field Equation."

- HTML: https://floatingpragma.io/oph/papers/from-observer-consensus-to-standard-physics/
- PDF: https://floatingpragma.io/oph/papers/from-observer-consensus-to-standard-physics/paper.pdf
- Release source: https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/releases/tag/r2022

The formal library contains more than 6,600 public Lean theorem and lemma declarations. The repository and paper release are the sources for exact counts, theorem statements, assumptions, and artifacts.

## AGI: Cadence

Cadence connects bounded observer-like patches with local state, declared ports, readback and repair. `TemporalPatchNet` learns observed paths by centered equilibrium detuning and carries context between observations. `TemporalMemory` protects selected acquired responses while learning continues in the remaining directions. The same learned model repairs continuous action proposals privately, and imagined continuations leave live activity, parameters and factual records unchanged. Retention capacity, importance selection and transfer between applications are bounded and stated with each result.

- Program overview: https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/
- Paper, with the controlled results and their assumptions (preprint on PhilPapers): https://philpapers.org/rec/MUECAP-2
- Library, MIT licensed: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence
- Documentation: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/main/docs/index.md
- Package: https://pypi.org/project/cadence-net/ (pip install cadence-net)
- Bundled Lean proofs, 169 conditional theorems: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/tree/main/lean

The proofs cover mathematical components and their limits. They do not certify the Python implementation or establish intelligence.

## Interpretation Boundary

The finite framework proves and computes results under displayed premises. Several bridges from finite objects to observed physics remain open or conditional. Diagnostic numerical agreements are not predictions when measured targets enter the construction or selection. The papers and scientific registers give the binding classification.
